87:1: The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of His statement, Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High. Some of them said: Its meaning is: glorify your Lord, the Most High, there is no Lord higher or greater than Him. And some of them, when they read that, would say: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Umar that he used to recite Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, Who created and proportioned. He said: And this is how Ubayy bin Ka’b read it. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Abd al-Khayr, who said: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, recite Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, and he said: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hamadani, that when Ibn Abbas recited Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, he would say: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. And when he recited I swear by the Day of Resurrection (al-Qiyamah 75:1) and came to the end of it, Is He not able to give life to the dead? (al-Qiyamah 75:40), he would say: Glory be to You, O God, and yes. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High. He told us that when the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it, he would say: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Kharijah, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Abdullah, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas recite in the Maghrib prayer: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High. Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: O Muhammad, purify the name of your Lord, the Most High, from naming anything other than Him by it. He is forbidding him from doing what the polytheists did, by naming some of their gods Al-Lat and some Al-Uzza. Others said: The meaning of this is: God is glorified from what the polytheists say about Him, as He said: And do not insult those they invoke other than God, lest they insult God in enmity without knowledge (al-An’am 6:108). They said: The meaning of this is: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High. They said: The name is not a meaning. Others said: He exalted your name, O Muhammad, and your mention of Him, so that you do not mention Him except while you are humble and submissive to Him. They said: What is meant by the name is the naming, but the name was placed in place of the source. Others said: The meaning of his saying: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High is: Pray in remembrance of your Lord, O Muhammad. He means by that: Pray while remembering Him, and fearing and dreading Him. The first and most correct of the sayings on this matter, in our view, is the saying of those who said: Its meaning is: glorify the name of your Lord, lest you call upon the gods and idols with it, based on what I mentioned of the reports, from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and from the Companions, that when they recited that, they would say: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. Thus, it is clear that its meaning was known to them: glorify the name of your Lord, and glorify Him.
87:2: And His saying: Who created and proportioned means: He who created things and proportioned their creation and made them equal, and proportioning is adjustment.
87:3: And His saying: And He Who has decreed and guided God Almighty says: And He Who has decreed and guided His creation. The commentators differed on the meaning intended by his saying He guided. Some of them said: He guided man to the path of good and evil, and the animals to pastures. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, He has decreed and guided, he said: He guided mankind to misery and happiness, and He guided livestock to their pastures. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: guiding males to the place where females are, and we have mentioned the narration about this previously. The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that God, by His statement So He guided, is general in the report of His guidance of His creation, and He did not specify one meaning over another. He guided them to the path of good and evil, and He guided the males to the path of females. So the report is general, until a report comes that establishes the proof, indicating its specificity. The reciters of the regions agreed to make the dal of qadr double, except for al-Kisa’i, who made it light. The correct thing to do is to emphasize it, because the evidence is unanimous on it.
87:4: And His saying: And He Who brought forth pasture means: And He Who brought forth from the earth pasture for livestock, from various kinds of plants and types of grass. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yaqub bin Makram told me, he said: Al-Hafri told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin, He brought out the pasture, he said: the plants. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And He who brought forth the pasture... the verse, plants as you have seen, between yellow, red, and white.
87:5: And His statement: Then He made it black stubble, God Almighty says: So He made that pasture stubble, which is what dried up from the plants and was blown away by the wind. What is meant by it here is that He made it dry chaff that changed to blackness, which is blackness, after the whiteness or greenness, from the intensity of the dryness. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, black stubble, he said: chaff that has changed. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, black scum, he said: The scum of the torrent is black, he said: black. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, black scum, he said: It returns to being dry after being green. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And He made it a dark stubble, he said: It was green grass and plants, then it became dry and became dark stubble, carried away by the winds and floods. Some of the people of knowledge of the Arabic language were of the view that this is from the deferred meaning of the advance, and that the meaning of the statement is: And He who brought forth the pasture dark: that is, green to black, then He made it dark stubble after that. And he based his statement on the statement of Dhu al-Rummah: Eve is ulcerated and has signs, and she has stopped going and the buds have surrounded her This statement, although it is not refuted that the Arabs call the plant that is extremely green black, is not correct in my opinion, as it is contrary to the interpretation of the people of interpretation, that the letter only uses trickery to achieve its intended meaning by advancing or delaying if it has no understood face except by advancing it from its place, or delaying it. But if it has a correct face in its place, then there is no reason to seek trickery for its meaning by advancing or delaying it.
87:6: And His saying: We will make you recite, and you will not forget, except what God wills. God Almighty says: We will make you recite, O Muhammad, this Qur’an, and you will not forget it, except what God wills. Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of His statement, So do not forget, except what God wills. Some of them said: This is God informing His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that He will teach him this Qur’an and will memorize it for him, and a prohibition from him to hasten to recite it, as He, the Most High, said, “Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation.” (al-Qiyamah 75:16-17) Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, We will make you recite, and you will not forget, he said: He used to remember the Qur’an in his heart for fear that he would forget. So those who said this statement said: The meaning of the exception in this place is about forgetting, and the meaning of the statement is: so you will not forget, except what God wills that you forget and not remember. They said: That is what God abrogated from the Qur’an, so He removed its ruling and its recitation. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: We will make you recite, and you will not forget. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not forget anything, except what God wills. Others said: The meaning of forgetting in this context is abandonment. They said: The meaning of the statement is: We will teach you, O Muhammad, so do not abandon working with any of it, except what God wills that you abandon working with from what He abrogated. Some of the Arab scholars used to say about this: God did not will that you forget anything, and it is like His saying: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills (Hud 11:107) and He does not will. He said: And you say about the sleeve: I will give you everything you asked for, except what you will, and unless I will to prevent you, and the intention is not to prevent it, and not to will anything. He said: And on this are the courses of faith, an exception is made in it, and the intention of the one who takes an oath: the one who touches. The statement that is more correct in my opinion is the statement of the one who said: The meaning of this is: Do not forget it unless we wish to make you forget it by abrogating it and removing it. We said that this is more correct, because it is the most obvious of its meanings.
87:7: God Almighty says: “Except what God wills. Indeed, He knows what is declared and what is hidden.” God Almighty says: God knows what is declared, O Muhammad, of your deeds, what you have made public and declared. And what is hidden. He says: And what is hidden from it that you have not made public and what you have concealed. He says: He knows all of your deeds, their secret and their public. He says: So beware of Him seeing you while you are acting in any of your circumstances in a way other than that which He has permitted you to do.
87:8: God Almighty says: And We make it easy for you, O Muhammad, to do good, which is ease, and ease is the verb from ease.
87:9: And His statement: Then remind, if the reminder should benefit, God Almighty says: So remind the servants of God, O Muhammad, of His greatness, admonish them, and warn them of His punishment. If the reminder should benefit, He says: If the reminder should benefit those whom you have despaired of ever believing, then the reminder should not benefit them. And His statement: Then remind, is a command from God to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to remind all people. Then He said: If the reminder should benefit those whom you have despaired of ever believing.
87:10: And His saying: He who fears will remember. God Almighty says: O Muhammad, if you remember those whom I have commanded you to remind, he who fears God and dreads His punishment will remember.
87:11: God Almighty says: And he avoids it meaning: And he avoids the reminder the most wretched meaning: the most wretched of the two groups. The one who will enter the Great Fire and they are those who are not benefited by the reminder. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, “So remember, if the reminder should benefit. He who fears will remember.” So fear God, no servant ever fears God except that he remembers Him. And the most wretched avoids it. No, by God, no servant avoids this remembrance out of asceticism and hatred for its people except that he is wretched in the midst of wretchedness.
87:12: And his saying: He who will enter the Great Fire means: He who will enter the fire of Hell, which is the Great Fire, and he means the Great Fire because of the intensity of the heat and pain.
87:13: And his saying: Then he will neither die therein nor live therein. He says: Then he will neither die in the Great Fire nor live therein, and that is because the soul of one of them will be in his throat therein, and it will not exit and leave him and he will die, nor will it return to its place in the body and he will live therein. And it was said: He will neither die therein and find rest, nor will he live a life that will benefit him. Others said: This was said because when the Arabs described a man as having fallen into extreme hardship, they would say: He is neither alive nor dead. So God addressed them with the same words that they used.
87:14: God Almighty says: He who purifies himself from disbelief and sins against God, and does what God has commanded him to do, and fulfills his obligations, will succeed and achieve his goal. A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said about this. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, meaning: He who purifies himself from polytheism. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Ansari told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, He has succeeded who purifies himself, he said: He whose deeds are pure. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: He has succeeded who purifies himself. He said: He acts out of piety. Saad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me: Hafs bin Omar Al-Adani told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding His statement, He has succeeded who purifies himself, meaning he who says, There is no god but God. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: He who pays the zakat on his wealth has succeeded. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Aqmar, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas: He has succeeded who purifies himself. He said: Whoever is able to bow down, let him do so, then let him stand and pray. Muhammad bin Amara Al-Razi told us, he said: Abu Naim told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Aqmar, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, He has succeeded who purifies himself, he said: He who submits. Muhammad bin Amara told us: Uthman bin Saeed bin Marra told us: Zuhair told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, who said: If a beggar comes to one of you while he wants to pray, let him give his zakat before his prayer, for God says: He has succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays. So whoever is able to give his zakat before his prayer, let him do so. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, He has succeeded who purifies himself, means a man purifies himself with his wealth and pleases his Creator. Others said: Rather, he meant Zakat al-Fitr. Who said that? Amr ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Amili narrated to me, saying: Marwan ibn Muawiyah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Khalda, who said: I entered upon Abu al-Aaliyah, and he said to me: When you go out tomorrow for the Eid, pass by me. So I passed by him, and he said: Have you eaten anything? I said: Yes. He said: Have you poured water over yourself? I said: Yes. He said: Then tell me what you did with your zakat? I said: I have spent it. He said: I only wanted you for this. Then he recited: Indeed he has succeeded who purifies himself, And remembers the name of his Lord and prays. And he said: The people of Madinah do not see a charity better than it, and than providing water to drink.
87:15: And his saying: And he mentioned the name of his Lord and prayed. The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying: And he mentioned the name of his Lord and prayed. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: He made God One. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And he mentioned the name of his Lord and prayed, meaning: He declared God Almighty to be One. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: He remembered God, called upon Him, and sought Him. The correct thing to say about this is: He mentioned God, made Him One, called upon Him, and called upon Him, because all of that is from the remembrance of God, and God Almighty did not specify one type of His remembrance over another. And his saying: So he prayed. The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that. Some of them said: What he meant by it is: So he prayed the five prayers. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, So he prayed, meaning: he prayed the five daily prayers. Others said: It means the Eid prayer on the day of Eid al-Fitr. Others said: Rather, what he meant by it is: And he mentioned the name of his Lord and supplicated. They said: The prayer here means supplication. The correct thing to say is: What he meant by his saying so he prayed is the prayers, and the remembrance of God in them through praise, glorification, and supplication.
87:16: And His saying: Rather, you prefer the life of this world. He is saying to the al-Nas 114:Rather, you, O people, prefer the adornments of the life of this world over the Hereafter.
87:17: God Almighty says: And the Hereafter is better for you and more lasting He says: The adornment of the Hereafter is better for you, O people, and more lasting, because worldly life is fleeting, while the Hereafter is everlasting; it will not end or perish. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Rather, you prefer the life of this world. So people chose the immediate life except for those whom God protected. And His statement: And the Hereafter is better in goodness, and more lasting in permanence. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Abu Hamza told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Urfajah Al-Thaqafi, who said: I asked Ibn Mas’ud to recite, Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, and when he reached, But you prefer the life of this world, he stopped reciting and turned to his companions and said: We prefer this world to the Hereafter. The people were silent, then he said: We prefer this world because we have seen its adornments, its women, its food and its drink, and the Hereafter has been turned away from us, so we have chosen this immediate life and abandoned the deferred life. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, Rather, you prefer the life of this world. The majority of the reciters of the regions recited it as Rather, you prefer with a ta’, except for Abu Amr, who recited it with a ya’, and said: He means the wretched. And I do not prefer him to read that with the ta’, because of the consensus of the proof from the reciters on it, and he mentioned that that is in Abu’s reading: Rather, you give preference, so that is also evidence of the correctness of the reading with the ta’.
87:18: And his saying: Indeed, this is in the former scriptures. The people of interpretation differed as to what was indicated by his saying this. Some of them said: It was indicated by the verses in Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah: Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses. He said: The verses in Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High. Others said: The story of this surah. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah: Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses. He said: The story of this surah is in the former scriptures. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: What God Almighty has narrated in this Surah is in the former scriptures. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, he said: Indeed, what God has related in this surah is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses. Others said: Rather, what he meant by that was that his saying, And the Hereafter is better and more lasting, was in the first scriptures. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, he said: The books of God have been written in succession as you hear, that the Hereafter is better and more lasting. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses, he said: In the scriptures that God sent down to Abraham and Moses: that the Hereafter is better than the first. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: His statement, “He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays. Rather, you prefer the life of this world, while the Hereafter is better and more lasting,” is in the first scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, and the scriptures of Moses, son of Imran. I said: This is more correct than others, because this is a reference to the present, so it is more appropriate for it to be a reference to what is close to it than a reference to something else. As for the scrolls: they are the plural of scroll, and what is meant by them is: the books of Abraham and Moses. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu al-Khald, he said: The scrolls of Abraham were revealed on the first night of Ramadan, the Torah was revealed six nights before Ramadan, the Psalms were revealed on twelve nights, the Gospel was revealed on eighteen, and the Criterion was revealed on twenty-four.
87:19: God Almighty says: The scrolls of Abraham and Moses.
